title: H 3157 (122nd General Assembly): Applications for Driver's License and Voter registration
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id) not stated.
(b_no_id_remedy) not stated.
(c_mail_ballot_id) not stated.
(d_proof_of_citizenship) not stated.
(e_other_rule) not stated.
(other) SECTION 1 (amends 7-5-320): a state ID card application or driver's license application (including renewal) given to the Department of Motor Vehicles counts as a voter registration application; the applicant consents to use of the signature already on the licence or ID card; the old rule that an unsigned form means declining is struck.
(other) Same section: a person who will be under 18 on the date of the next election has name and identifying information kept out of public records.
(other) Same section: the county board must notify each person how to decline; if the person does not decline within fifteen calendar days of the notice, the registration is complete.
(other) Same section: change-of-address form for a licence or ID card also updates voter registration unless the elector says otherwise; the State Election Commission and DMV executive directors must work together on compliance.
(other) SECTION 2: takes effect upon approval by the Governor.
(other) version: 2016-12-15_Introduced (only version): no slot a-d text; DMV automatic-registration text, same as the 2015 versions apart from a comma and sub-item numbering.
(other) note: Automatic-registration-through-DMV bill; no ID-to-vote, no no-ID remedy, no mail-ballot ID, and no proof-of-citizenship text. The only citizenship words are the existing statement that the registration form lists each eligibility requirement 'including citizenship', reprinted unchanged in 7-5-320(C)(2)(c)(i). One version. Substance is the same as H 3978 (2015).
(note) Off this topic: the bill sets no ID or citizenship-proof rule.
